title: Protocol for generation of transmitochondrial cybrids using a microfluidic device
author: Wada, Hosokawa, et al.

steps.title: Generate ρ0 recipient cells
steps.instruction: Culture 143B cells in ethidium bromide (EtBr) medium for 30–60 days, replacing the medium daily and maintaining the culture for at least 1 month until mtDNA is completely lost.

steps.title: Verify mtDNA depletion
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from the cultured 143B cells and perform PCR to confirm the absence of mtDNA; if mtDNA is detected, discard the cells and restart the ρ0 preparation.

steps.title: Introduce optional marker genes
steps.instruction: If desired, transduce or transfect the established ρ0 143B cells with additional marker genes before proceeding.

steps.title: Transfect donor and recipient cells
steps.instruction: Stably transfect HeLa cells (donor, TK⁺) with a puromycin‑resistant construct (H2B‑EGFP‑IRES‑Pur) and ρ0 143B cells (recipient, TK⁻) with a hygromycin‑resistant construct (H2B‑mCherry‑IRES‑Hyg) using a standard protocol; introduce any further marker genes if required.

steps.title: Cryopreserve ρ0 cells
steps.instruction: Freeze the generated ρ0 143B cells in a standard cryopreservation medium at –80 °C, then transfer to liquid‑nitrogen gas phase for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Design and order photomask
steps.instruction: Create CAD drawings for the alignment mark, first‑layer microtunnels, and second‑layer cell‑pairing structures (CPSs) and export as dwg files (Mask #4, #20, #27); order a glass (chrome) photomask from a manufacturer, allowing several days for delivery.

steps.title: Prepare silicon wafer
steps.instruction: Cut a silicon wafer into 32 × 32 mm squares; sonicate in isopropanol for 1 min, then in ultrapure water for 1 min; spin‑dry at 3000 rpm for 1 min and bake at 140 °C for 1 h in a clean dry oven (do not use a PDMS oven).

steps.title: Apply first SU‑8 layer
steps.instruction: Plasma‑etch the wafer with O₂ (20 Pa, 150 W, 15 min); spin‑coat S1805 at 3000 rpm for 25 s; bake at 120 °C for 1 min; align the photomask (alignment mark) on a mask aligner; expose to UV for 5 s; develop by shaking in NMD‑3 for 1 min then ultrapure water for 1 min; spin‑dry at 3000 rpm for 1 min and bake at 120 °C for 3 min; engrave the alignment mark with O₂ plasma (6 Pa, 100 W, 1 min), SF₃ plasma (20 Pa, 200 W, 1 min), then O₂ plasma (20 Pa, 150 W, 15 min).

steps.title: Create first microtunnel layer
steps.instruction: Spin‑coat SU‑8 5 at 7000 rpm for 15 s to obtain a ~2 µm layer; bake at 90 °C for 1 h; align the microtunnel photomask and expose to UV for 10 s; develop by shaking in SU‑8 developer for 5 min, then IPA for 2 min, spin‑dry at 3000 rpm for 1 min.

steps.title: Create second CPS layer
steps.instruction: Spin‑coat SU‑8 25 at 2500 rpm for 15 s to obtain a 26–28 µm layer; bake at 90 °C for 1 h; align the CPS/main‑channel photomask and expose to UV for 10 s; develop as in step 9; bake at 140 °C for 10 min; cool slowly to 20–25 °C by stopping heating and leaving the oven closed for several hours.

steps.title: Inspect and optionally fluorinate master
steps.instruction: Examine the fabricated CPS pattern under a microscope; if desired, fluorinate the silicon surface by plasma treating with CHF₃/O₂ (20 Pa, 200 W, 5 min) followed by CHF₃ alone (20 Pa, 200 W, 2 min) to reduce PDMS adhesion.

steps.title: Cast PDMS master mold
steps.instruction: Mix PDMS oligomer and curing agent at a 10:1 (w/w) ratio; place the master mold in a 60 mm dish and pour ~6 g of the mixture; degas under vacuum until bubbles disappear; cure at 65 °C for >1 h; cut along the wafer edge and peel off the cured PDMS to reveal the SU‑8 pattern.

steps.title: Prepare inlet reservoir tubes
steps.instruction: Cut 5 mm‑inner‑diameter silicone tubing to a length of 5–7 mm; store the pieces in 100 % ethanol; air‑dry before use.

steps.title: Fabricate PDMS chips
steps.instruction: Mix fresh PDMS (10:1); pour onto the master to a thickness of ~2 mm (1.4–1.6 g); degas; cure at 65 °C for >1 h; cut along the wafer edge, peel off the chip, and place it on a clean glass slip; repeat to produce the required number of chips (hundreds can be made from one master).

steps.title: Punch inlet and outlet holes
steps.instruction: Using a biopsy trepan, punch a 2 mm‑diameter hole for the inlet and another for the outlet in each PDMS chip.

steps.title: Bond silicone tubes to inlet
steps.instruction: Apply uncured PDMS mixture to the cut surface of the silicone tube; insert the tube into the inlet hole; bake the assembly at 100 °C for >1 h (optional 12–24 h) to fully cure and sterilize the bond.

steps.title: Assemble microfluidic device
steps.instruction: Place the PDMS chip (with bonded inlet tube) onto a 35 mm culture dish; cover with a lid; avoid re‑placing the chip or plasma‑treating it, as reversible bonding is required.

steps.title: Store prepared devices
steps.instruction: Keep the assembled microfluidic devices under normal atmospheric conditions for at least several weeks before use.

steps.title: Extract bulk DNA for PCR
steps.instruction: Harvest 2–5 × 10⁵ cells; lyse in 500–1000 µL proteinase K solution at 55 °C for >6 h; heat at 95 °C for 10 min; dilute the lysate 10‑fold with milliQ water.

steps.title: Prepare single‑cell PCR template
steps.instruction: Melt 0.5 % agarose in water; add 1 mL to a 100 mm dish and spread; cool to 20–25 °C, then incubate at 55 °C until completely dry; add 10–15 mL PBS to the agarose‑coated dish, spread for ~6 h; finally heat at 95 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Run PCR for mtDNA
steps.instruction: Prepare a 20 µL reaction containing 1 µL KOD polymerase, 0.4 µL forward primer (10 µM), 0.6 µL reverse primer (10 µM), 2 µL 10× KOD buffer, 2 µL 2 mM dNTPs, 0.8 µL 25 mM MgSO₄, and 12.6 µL water; add 1 µL DNA template; cycle: 94 °C 2 min; 98 °C 10 s (30–40 cycles); 68 °C 3 min; final extension 68 °C 7 min; hold at 16 °C.

steps.title: Digest PCR products
steps.instruction: Mix 2 µL PCR product with 10 µL SspI working solution; incubate at 37 °C for >1 h.

steps.title: Electrophorese and stain DNA
steps.instruction: Run the digested samples on a 1.0–1.5 % agarose gel using a standard electrophoresis protocol; stain the gel with ethidium bromide for 1 h at 20–25 °C; image the gel to identify the 1,854 bp (HeLa) or 1,289 bp (143B) fragments.
